events.title: The Seventeenth Council of Toledo orders the enslavement of Jews
events.description: Accusing Jews of conspiracy, the council called by King Egica decreed the enslavement of Jews in Visigothic Spain and the removal of their children. It was among the harshest anti-Jewish measures of the early Middle Ages.
events.html: Accusing Jews of conspiracy, the council called by King Egica decreed the enslavement of Jews in Visigothic Spain and the removal of their children. It was among the harshest anti-Jewish measures of the early Middle Ages.

events.title: Napoleon's coup of 18 Brumaire topples the Directory
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte and his allies began a coup against the Directory, completed the next day. The new Consulate made Napoleon First Consul and effective ruler of France.
events.html: Napoleon Bonaparte and his allies began a coup against the Directory, completed the next day. The new Consulate made Napoleon First Consul and effective ruler of France.

events.title: Wilhelm II's abdication is announced as Germany becomes a republic
events.description: With revolution spreading, Chancellor Max von Baden announced the Kaiser's abdication and Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a republic in Berlin. Wilhelm fled to the Netherlands the next day.
events.html: With revolution spreading, Chancellor Max von Baden announced the Kaiser's abdication and Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a republic in Berlin. Wilhelm fled to the Netherlands the next day.

events.title: Kristallnacht: Nazi pogroms sweep Germany and Austria
events.description: Over two nights, Nazi mobs burned hundreds of synagogues, wrecked about 7,500 Jewish businesses and killed at least 91 people. About 30,000 Jewish men were sent to concentration camps.
events.html: Over two nights, Nazi mobs burned hundreds of synagogues, wrecked about 7,500 Jewish businesses and killed at least 91 people. About 30,000 Jewish men were sent to concentration camps.

events.title: The Berlin Wall opens
events.description: After a confused announcement that East Germans could travel freely, crowds pressed the border crossings until guards opened the gates. The fall of the Wall led to German reunification within a year.
